Maintenance Report — MNT-0170-003

Asset: WELL-0170 (NE-08 Well 170, T200, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: downhole pump Work started: 08 Jul 2023 08:00 · Finished: 17 Jul 2023 23:00 · Well stopped for this job: 231 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Kevin Price · Contractor: Sandstone Rod & Pump Triggered by: inspection INS-0170-0037 on 2023-07-06 Report written: 19 Jul 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that the wellhead was cold and the pump jack was straining with a heavy, uneven load. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0170-0037 showed the wellhead at 39.2 °C with the air at 37.1 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The downhole pump was stuck, most likely from sand or scale. Sandstone Rod & Pump's workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 8 days for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

Root cause

A worn plunger that let sand settle and lock the pump.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rods and the insert pump.
  3. Inspected the pump: sand in the barrel and a worn plunger.
  4. Ran in a new insert pump.
  5. Re-spaced the pump and hung the rods back on.

Summary of the fix: pulled and replaced downhole pump.

Testing and return to service

Pump test confirmed fluid to surface and the wellhead warmed back to normal. The well was returned to production.

Asset: WELL-0170 (NE-08 Well 170, T200, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: flowline Work started: 25 Aug 2023 08:00 · Finished: 26 Aug 2023 12:00 · Well stopped for this job: 28 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Kevin Price · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. What happened

The weekly manual inspection INS-0170-0044 at 14:30 on 2023-08-24 found crude oil on the pad: about 3.2% of the pad area, estimated 0.9 bbl. The inspector noted: "Oil sheen around cellar." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 8.7 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to the flanged flowline connection at the wellhead cellar.

Root cause

A failed gasket on the flange where the flowline leaves the wellhead.

Field staff reported that the motor breaker kept tripping and the pump jack would not run. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0170-0079 showed the wellhead at 27.0 °C with the air at 23.6 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. An insulation test showed a winding fault, so the motor was replaced with an exchange unit. Winding breakdown from heat and age.

What happened

Field staff reported that the pumper heard grinding from the walking beam and saw the horsehead wobbling. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0170-0202 showed the wellhead at 34.2 °C with the air at 32.0 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing. The well is expected to stay shut in for about 37 days longer than the repair itself because the replacement part is back-ordered from the supplier.

Grease contaminated with sand had worn the bearing.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 1 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done so far

  1. Lowered the horsehead and supported the walking beam with a crane.
  2. Removed the saddle bearing assembly.

Still to do: complete the remaining repair steps, test the equipment and return the well to production.

Summary of the fix: replaced saddle bearing and re-greased.

Testing and return to service

Not done yet. The work is expected to finish on 28 Oct 2026; testing and return to service will be recorded in the final report.
